messages:
ashley: Heads-up — after the canary this morning I'm seeing a tail latency regression on tool-calling traffic. 95th/99th up ~60-90ms. Perf monitor flagged it at 08:12. Repro'd with local stress harness.
devon: ugh. Is this only on flows that do tool/function calls or broader?
ashley: narrowed to toolcall + structured-output routes. Non-tool flows look stable. Attaching short perf dump and scheduler trace below.
ashley: ```
batch formation: N=8 avg_fill=3.1
event: request A -> enters batch
event: request B -> enters batch
event: request A -> paused for tool (external I/O), batch emitted early -> split
profiler: kernel_select: fp16_conv -> switched to fallback_kernel at step+4 (higher latency)
kv-cache: eviction spikes during pause windows (approx 12 evictions/s)
``` 
priya: interesting — batch is splintering when one request pauses for toolcall, leaving partial batches behind. that triggers kernel recompile/selection on the remaining fragment, which explains the kernel_select flip.
ben: can you paste the exact deploy id? might be a runtime tweak that changed batching thresholds.
ashley: deploy-bot shows: infra-batch-optim v2026.03.08-canary -> applied to canary nodes. infra-bot: <@infra-bot> rolled infra-batch-optim:v2026.03.08 to canary at 07:58 :rocket:
devon: ok probable culprit. Two angles: (1) make queue policy more pause-aware so paused requests don't force premature emission, (2) reduce sensitivity of kernel selection to tiny sequence-length deltas (avoid recompile on small splits).
priya: agree. quick mitigations to test:
- raise token_budget_target from 0.6 -> 0.75 for toolcall routes (more willing to wait to fill)
- set hold_window_ms: 25 -> 40 for those routes (shorter than happy-path latency budget but helps coalesce)
- implement soft-pin of KV cache for requests that were recently preempted (reduce eviction during pause)
ben: config snippets:
```yaml
routes:
  - match: path:/v1/generate/tool
    batching:
      token_budget_target: 0.75
      hold_window_ms: 40
      treat_tool_pauses_as_nonpreemptive: true
``` 
devon: also add metrics to validate: batch_splits_by_toolpause, kv_evictions_during_pause, kernel_switch_ratio. Grafana query: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd/toolcall-batches
ashley: I applied the config change to canary pool (1 node) and kicked off our synthetic load. Early numbers: p95 reduced by ~35ms vs canary before, p99 improved ~50ms. Cost up a hair due to longer wait times for some requests.
priya: nice. Did the kernel_switch_ratio go down?
ashley: yes — kernel_switch_ratio dropped from 0.18 -> 0.05 on synthetic. kv_evictions_during_pause also halved. Full metrics here: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd/compare
ben: for structured output flows we should also look at stop token behavior: sometimes model emits stop early which finalizes a request and leaves other batch members with less context -> more splits. we could change structured-output to emit explicit EOS marker instead of relying on stop sequences so the router treats completion deterministically.
devon: good point. proposal: add `finalize_on_eos_only: true` for structured routes and keep stop-seq handling in a fallback tier. That avoids mid-decode early finalize.
priya: small note: function/toolcall semantics currently cause synchronous blocking in the decode path. If we can background the tool invocation and let decoding continue with a placeholder token sequence, we might keep batch continuity at cost of some additional complexity in output merging.
ashley: that's a bigger change but we can spike it. short term: keep the config changes and run 1% A/B on dedicated. ben — can you schedule the A/B on dedicated pool? devon takes infra knobs for kernel sensitivity rollback if needed.
ben: scheduled. A/B 1% traffic, 2h run, dedicated-pool-3. I'll post results.
infra-bot: <@ben> created A/B experiment ab-test-1970012345 in experiments-db (id: exp-1970012345). Started at 09:21.
devon: next steps for this thread:
- ashley: collect full perf traces and attach
- priya: prepare the finalize_on_eos_only PR (small flag toggle)
- ben: run A/B and share metrics
- infra: brief rollback plan if kernel regression reappears
ashley: ack. attaching trace export to comments and will update when A/B done. thanks all :thumbsup:
priya: nice detective work. small doc idea: write up a short playbook for "toolpause-induced batch splintering" so oncall has steps.
ashley: will draft it after results. closing notes: this looks like a behavioral regression introduced by batching heuristics; mitigations show promising gains. we'll keep monitoring.
